chunks: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Zanjani informed me in what he wrote to me, saying: Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: I heard Qasim ibn Salam say:

Regarding the meaning of the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family): 'The womb is a shujna from Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He,' he means that it is a kinship that is interlocked like the interlocking of veins. And the saying of the speaker: 'The narration has shujun' is that some parts of it adhere to others. And some of the people of knowledge said: It is said: 'A tree that is mutashajjin' if some of its branches wrap around each other. And it is said: shujna and shujna, and al-shajn is like a branch that is from the tree. And the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) has said: Indeed, Fatima is a shujna from me; that which hurts her, hurts me, and that which makes her happy, makes me happy. May the prayers of Allah be upon her.

key_terms.ذُو شُجُونٍ: Having shujun; having intertwined or connected parts
key_terms.شَجْنَةٌ: Shujna; an interlocked or entangled part, used metaphorically for close kinship
key_terms.شَجْنَةٌ مِنِّي: A shujna from me; indicating a close, intertwined spiritual and familial bond
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ: Fatima; the daughter of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'shujna' in the hadith about the womb and Fatima?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq elucidates the etymology of 'shujna' as interlocked branches or veins, grounding the spiritual concept of kinship in tangible linguistic imagery. This explanation underscores the profound metaphysical bond between the Prophet and Fatima (peace be upon her), illustrating how her experiences are an extension of his own, a key tenet in Shia theology regarding the Ahl al-Bayt's unique status.
